dedupe_keys.name: toddbrook reservoir auxiliary spillway failure whaley bridge england august 2019

description: This case study covers the 1 August 2019 failure of the concrete auxiliary spillway at Toddbrook Reservoir above Whaley Bridge in Derbyshire, an embankment of about 80 feet built in 1837 to 1840 and owned by the Canal & River Trust since 2012. After a week of well-forecast heavy rain in two events, the second about a 1 percent annual probability, chute slabs collapsed into a void and about 1,500 people were evacuated while the reservoir was drawn down. The independent review found the chute lacked underdrains, water injected through a joint liquefied the shoulder fill into a slurry that lifted the slabs, and that a flood much smaller than the probable maximum flood caused it, although the reservoir met existing legislation; it made 22 recommendations, over half for new industry guidance. Coverage: one dam, a detailed timeline and mechanism. Access: free web page and PDF; the review is under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Caveats: findings are those of the panel, and the ASDSO page summarises them. It supports spillway fragility and dam emergency modelling, and relates to the Oroville spillway forensic review and ASDSO emergency warning lessons in the catalogue.
